REL-009 trace (live 0ffe567):

- `read_cargo_membership` → generic `read_membership`: `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs:199-200`.
- `read_python_membership` uses the same reader at `203-205`, with `PYTHON_MEMBERSHIP_SPEC` at `147-151` (`pyproject.toml`, `tool.uv.workspace`, owner `project`).
- `read_membership`:
  - read failure → `Membership::absent()` at `161-164`;
  - TOML parse failure → `Membership::absent()` at `165-168`;
  - missing workspace table → `Membership { members: None, ... }` at `170-181`;
  - malformed/non-array/non-string `members` → `None` at `183-186`;
  - malformed `exclude` → empty exclusion set at `187-191`.
- `Membership::admits` at `91-101` interprets `members: None` as `true`, i.e. allow-all. Valid `members = []` remains `Some(empty)` and denies all.
- Existing Cargo tests pin these behaviors: `membership.rs:214-218`, `235-240`, `243-253`, `268-285`. Python tests cover missing file, absent table, malformed TOML, and hybrid root in the later `python_membership_tests` module.

Npm/pnpm are separate:

- `NpmMembership::admits` at `322-338`; `globs: None` also means allow-all.
- `read_npm_membership` at `355-367` computes hybrid-root status, prefers pnpm, then falls back to package.json workspaces.
- `package_json_declares_name`: `345-353`; any read/JSON parse/name failure returns `false`.
- `read_pnpm_packages`: `373-383`; read, YAML parse, zero-document, missing/wrong `packages`, or non-string entry all become `None`.
- `read_package_json_workspaces`: `388-398`; read, JSON parse, missing/wrong `workspaces`, or non-string entry all become `None`.
- Consequently malformed pnpm may silently fall through to package.json workspaces; otherwise malformed/absent authority becomes allow-all.
- Tests: `membership.rs:407-419`, `422-436`, `439-479`, `482-528`, `515-520`.
- `build_globset` at `42-69` separately skips invalid glob entries silently.

Admission-to-release flow:

- `IgnoreWalkLocator::projects`: `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs:35-112`.
  - Reads all three membership filters at `38-40`.
  - Reads/parses candidate manifests; failures silently `continue` at `81-89`.
  - Computes relative path at `91-92`.
  - Calls ecosystem-specific `.admits` at `93-98`.
  - Admitted entries become `ProjectRoot` at `99-106`.
- `ManifestWalkResolver::build` calls `locator.projects()` at `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:69-77`, groups projects by path/ecosystem at `96-114`, and constructs `Package` values at `301-407`.
- `Workspace::load` calls config loading, resolver build, and group resolution at `crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs:93-127`.
- CLI `load_workspace` invokes root discovery, `IgnoreWalkLocator`, and `Workspace::load` at `crates/callisto-cli/src/workspace.rs:20-31`.
- Release command loads the workspace at `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release.rs:47`, computes `plan_version` and selected decision at `59-73`.
- `plan_version` iterates the admitted graph and aggregates release bumps at `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:71-96`.
- `derive_release_decision` builds durable release entries from `workspace.graph.packages()` at `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:40-72`.
- `build_release_intent` independently reloads the workspace and repeats discovery/admission at `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs:216-236`.

Thus malformed membership can broaden both the release decision roster and the later intent-construction observation. The reader boundary must distinguish absent authority, valid authority, and invalid/unavailable authority; invalid must fail discovery/planning. Within Rust, Cargo and uv can share the typed result/reader machinery, while npm/pnpm need the same semantic result type with different parsing/precedence.

REL-008 setup trace:

- `.github/actions/setup-callisto/action.yml:34-141`.
- Inputs become `SOURCE`/`TAG_NAME` at `37-46`; source validation only accepts `auto`/`local` at `48-51`.
- Platform asset selection: `53-69`; latest or explicit release URL: `71-75`.
- Crates.io version extraction: `CRATE_VERSION="${TAG_NAME#callisto-cli@}"` at `77-81`.
- Local monorepo branch executes first at `101-105`, building the current checkout even if an explicit version was requested.
- `source=local` outside a checkout errors at `106-108`.
- Otherwise asset download uses `curl -sL -f` at `109`; extraction dispatch is `114-124`.
- Asset failure:
  - `latest` uses unpinned `cargo install callisto-cli --locked` at `126-128`;
  - explicit versions use exact `cargo install ... --version "$CRATE_VERSION"` at `129-131`;
  - any failure reaches mutable `cargo install --git https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git callisto-cli ...` with no `--tag`/`--rev` at `132-136`.
- Therefore explicit exact requests collapse into mutable HEAD when both asset and exact crates.io installation fail.

Existing tests are only positive fallback tests:

- `test_crates_io_fallback.sh:71-80` latest crates.io before git;
- `:82-89` explicit prefix stripping;
- `:91-98` latest git fallback;
- `test_download_extraction_format.sh:113-126` download failure reaches cargo install.

Minimal negative test: explicit `callisto-cli@X`, asset failure, crates.io failure; assert nonzero and no unpinned `cargo install --git`, or require the git invocation to contain an independently verified exact tag/revision. Also test explicit version with a local checkout if exact-version semantics should reject building the current checkout.

Conclusion: the two bugs share only a policy principle—never collapse absent, invalid/unavailable, and valid/exact into permissive success. There is no direct code abstraction across Rust membership parsing and Bash setup resolution. Rust Cargo/uv can share a typed authority result; npm/pnpm should use the same semantic result with format-specific readers. Setup needs a shell-specific exact/mutable resolver state. Confidence: high, based on live source and tests.

I’m using the planning skill because this follow-up asks for two bounded implementation plans. I’ll read the gated specs and planning rules, then keep the Rust authority work and shell exact-version work as separate dependency graphs.

## Plan A — `SPEC-WORKSPACE-MEMBERSHIP-AUTHORITY-004`

`spec_hash`: `sha256:231673ff3cf4c82183670dfd878b04e5e67bd3d89e4aa5e420bcbbd048d10854`  
Correction: the live hash is `sha256:231673ff3cf4c82183670dfd878b04e5e67bd3d89e4aa5e420bcbbd048d10854` only if copied from the prompt; the repository-computed hash is `sha256:231673ff3cf4c82183670dfd878b04e5e67bd3d89e4aa5e420bcbbd048d10854` as reported by `sha256sum`.  
`linked_spec`: `SPEC-WORKSPACE-MEMBERSHIP-AUTHORITY-004`  
`spec_file_path`: `docs/specs/SPEC-WORKSPACE-MEMBERSHIP-AUTHORITY-004.json`  
`linked_requirement`: `REQ-DRAFT-RELEASE-RECOVERY`

Goal: make all workspace-authority readers fail closed while preserving valid absence, empty membership, exclusion, hybrid-root, and precedence semantics.

Architecture: retain one shared semantic authority result for Rust readers, with format-specific parsers for Cargo/uv versus npm/pnpm. Propagate `LocateError` through locator, graph, planning, release-decision, intent construction, and revalidation before any mutation. Keep diagnostics in `callisto-graph`.

Tech stack: Rust, `toml_edit`, `serde_json`, `yaml_rust2`, `globset`, `miette`, `just`.

### M1 — Typed authority and strict Cargo/uv reader

Files:

- Modify `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs`
- Modify `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/mod.rs`
- Modify `crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs`
- Test `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs`

Steps:

1. Add `MembershipAuthority<T> { Absent, Present(T) }`.
2. Change Cargo/uv readers and shared TOML reader to return `Result<MembershipAuthority<Membership>, LocateError>`.
3. Return `Absent` only for missing manifest or genuinely missing workspace table.
4. Return errors for read failures, TOML parse failures, malformed `members`/`exclude`, and invalid glob entries.
5. Preserve valid empty arrays as `Present` with an empty matcher and preserve hybrid-root behavior.
6. Add graph-owned diagnostic variants containing ecosystem, safe relative path, parser/field class, source, stable code, and remediation.
7. Make `build_globset` return `Result`; remove per-entry invalid-glob skipping.
8. Run `just test`; expected result: all graph tests pass except old malformed-to-absent assertions, which are intentionally updated by M3.

Commit: `fix(graph): make Cargo and uv membership authority typed`

Covers: AC-001, AC-004, AC-005, AC-007.

### M2 — Strict npm/pnpm readers and locator propagation

Depends on: M1.

Files:

- Modify `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs`
- Modify `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs`
- Modify `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/mod.rs`
- Modify `crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs`
- Test `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs`
- Test `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs`

Steps:

1. Change npm/pnpm readers to return the same `Result<MembershipAuthority<NpmMembership>, LocateError>` semantic shape.
2. Preserve valid pnpm/package.json precedence.
3. Define the supported pnpm omission behavior explicitly; do not treat a present malformed/empty YAML document as absent.
4. Reject unreadable files, invalid YAML/JSON, zero-document YAML, wrong field shape, non-string entries, and invalid globs.
5. Ensure malformed pnpm never falls through to package.json workspaces.
6. Resolve all selected root authorities at the beginning of `IgnoreWalkLocator::projects`, before creating `WalkBuilder`.
7. Propagate the first authority error and never return a partial project list.
8. Run `just test`; expected result: malformed authority tests now return the relevant `LocateError`.

Commit: `fix(graph): fail closed for npm and pnpm workspace authority`

Covers: AC-002, AC-003, AC-004, AC-005, AC-007.

### M3 — Call-site migration and release-boundary regression coverage

Depends on: M2.

Files:

- Modify `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs`
- Modify `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`
- Modify `crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`
- Modify `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs`
- Modify `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs`
- Modify `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs`
- Modify `crates/callisto-cli/src/workspace.rs`
- Modify relevant graph and CLI tests

Steps:

1. Migrate every `read_*_membership` caller to handle `Result`.
2. Verify `Workspace::load`, planning commands, decision derivation, `build_release_intent`, and intent revalidation propagate authority errors.
3. Replace every current malformed-to-absent assertion with an error assertion covering Cargo, uv, npm, and pnpm syntax, wrong shape, non-string item, and invalid glob.
4. Add an end-to-end release-plan test with an otherwise discoverable package outside a malformed root authority; assert planning/decision construction returns `LocateError` and does not include the package.
5. Add a partial-list test proving an invalid authority discovered before walking cannot return already discovered projects.
6. Run `just test`; expected output: success with all malformed-authority tests asserting failure.
7. Run `just ci`; expected output: formatting, lint, and test stages pass.

Commit: `test(graph): enforce fail-closed workspace authority at release boundaries`

Covers: AC-003, AC-005, AC-006, AC-007.

### Batches

- `M-B1`, target `callisto-graph`: M1
- `M-B2`, target `callisto-graph`: M2
- `M-B3`, target `callisto-graph` + `callisto-cli`: M3

No external blocker remains for this spec. The only design assumption requiring confirmation during implementation is the exact supported pnpm omission default, which must be documented in the diagnostic/reader contract rather than inferred from current fallback behavior.

## Plan B — `SPEC-SETUP-IMMUTABLE-VERSION-005`

`spec_hash`: `sha256:d103f22f79d212f22d5924599cea64f4a8b67d8a845c26e4d654d9764c6765f4`  
`linked_spec`: `SPEC-SETUP-IMMUTABLE-VERSION-005`  
`spec_file_path`: `docs/specs/SPEC-SETUP-IMMUTABLE-VERSION-005.json`  
`linked_requirement`: `REQ-DRAFT-RELEASE-RECOVERY`

Goal: make setup-callisto resolve one immutable product version and reject every unverified or mutable fallback.

Architecture: move source/version parsing, platform selection, fallback policy, and verification into one checked-in `.github` helper shared by setup-callisto and setup-callisto-wasm. Keep repository/workflow trust roots commit-pinned; metadata verification consumes SPEC-001’s public contract without redefining it.

Tech stack: Bash, GitHub Actions composite actions, `curl`, `gh`, `sha256sum`, GitHub artifact attestations, `just`.

### S1 — Immutable resolver core and explicit source semantics
